Sam: Heads up — saw a perf regression on the paged-flash path when running large batches with interleaved KV + bf16. ~12% tail latency increase vs baseline. cc @Liz @Tariq
Liz: Which model/seq/batch? do you have the profiler dump?
Sam: mpt-30b, seq=2048, batch=24. Quick flame/prof below. Repro is consistent across two runs.
Sam: ```
-- kernel timeline (ms) --
flash_paged_forward: 18.9
flash_fused_forward: 16.3
kv_load_stalls: 12.7
memcpy_async_wait: 3.1
-- note: tail spikes at 95th, visible in flash_paged_forward
```
Tariq: That looks like bank/warp conflict amplification from interleaved layout + bf16 packing. If you switch to separate-KV layout does the tail go away?
Sam: Re-ran with separate layout: tail back to baseline (within noise). So interleaved layout is the trigger. Repro command: `python tools/repro/attn_kv_stride.py --model mpt-30b --layout interleaved --dtype bf16 --batch 24`
Ana: Quick fix idea: change kernel selector to prefer the fused/paged variant based on (dtype, stride alignment, batch). E.g. if dtype==bf16 && (kv_stride % warp_size) != 0 then prefer paged-flash that does explicit padding. Also add a safety fallback when tail increases >10%.
Kevin: Agreed on selector rule, but we should gate with a microbenchmark in CI that exercises interleaved+bf16 across batch sizes [8,16,24,32] so we catch regressions. I can add the bench and a perf presubmit.
Tariq: I'll prototype selector patch. Pseudo: ```diff
- if (seq_density > threshold) use_fused=true;
+ if (dtype==bf16 && kv_stride % 32 != 0) use_fused=false;
```
Sam: Also observed this only when batch >= 20 and seq>=1024. For small batches no difference. Might be worth encoding batch threshold in heuristic.
Kevin: @ci-bot can you spin up a regression run for label=kv-interleave-bf16 so we have baseline numbers?
ci-bot: Triggered perf/regression suite with tag=kv-interleave-bf16; run id=2026-03-18_01. Will post artifacts to build/2334819200 when complete.
Liz: Next steps: Tariq implements selector heuristic + unit bench, Kevin wires CI job, Sam drafts short RFC describing interleaved vs separate risk matrix and fallback policy. Goal: patch + CI bench by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
